A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ActiveGAMER paper, including all 19 pages and supplementary material. Text extraction and rendering support a complete comparison; the only visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated active-mapping experiments on Replica and MP3D, including reconstruction, rendering, ablation, runtime and per-scene results in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original Replica and MP3D experiments, ablations, runtime measurements and supplementary results in Tables 1–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 are identical, retaining Gaussian mapping, rendering-based planning, coarse-to-fine exploration, global-local keyframe selection and post-refinement.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate active reconstruction and novel-view rendering on the same Replica and MP3D scenes, including the supplementary evaluations and trajectories in Section 9.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 1 includes FBE, UPEN, OccAnt, ANM and NARUTO; Table 2 includes SplaTAM and NARUTO. The supplementary comparisons in Tables 5–7 also match.

E3.justification: The protocols remain identical, including 2000 steps for Replica, 5000 for MP3D, 680 × 1200 RGB-D inputs, evaluation metrics, rendering masks and selection of exploration versus refinement models.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Section 4.3, reconstruction-progress analysis in Figure 5, runtime analysis, trajectory visualizations and failure cases in the supplementary material are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain identical scene averages, runtime averages and candidate-information distributions in Figure 5. Neither adds seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and qualitative findings match. For example, both report MP3D accuracy of 1.66 cm and completion ratio of 95.32% in Table 1, and average Replica PSNR of 32.02 dB in Table 2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), including Gaussian rendering, optimization, densification and information gain, are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain identical contributions and claims concerning rendering-based exploration, unrestricted 6DoF movement, geometric completeness and photometric fidelity.

C2.justification: The post-refinement tradeoff between rendering quality and geometric completeness is unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning known localization, action execution, motion constraints, near-surface viewpoints and double-sided objects.

D1.justification: Section 7 retains identical hardware, memory-use, optimization-iteration and densification-resolution details. Implementation settings and resource-access information are unchanged throughout.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 76 references are unchanged, including positioning relative to NeRF methods, SplaTAM, NARUTO, ActiveSplat and AG-SLAM.

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2501.06897v1 dated 12 Jan 2025 to v2 dated 1 Apr 2025. All other extracted text, terminology, headings and document structure are identical.

P2.justification: All nine figures, seven tables, captions and placements are unchanged. Rendered pages 2–19 are pixel-identical; the first-page difference is confined to the version/date stamp, with no layout revision.

improvement.justification: The scientific text, results, supplementary analyses, reproducibility information and visual presentation are unchanged. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful difference in the paper's overall quality.
